name: Limited Save
description: Ink-ribbon saving: each manual save consumes a finite token held in the inventory, so 'should I save now' becomes the same species of decision as 'should I heal now' — and in this genre, deciding wrong is content. The write itself is delegated to persistence.save_system; durability, slots, and corruption handling are solved there, and this component is a gate on WHEN save_system may fire plus the token bookkeeping. Requiring a save-point location is config, not law, but the default holds it because save-anywhere plus scarce tokens is just a harder difficulty setting, while save-rooms are pacing architecture. Autosaves and setpiece checkpoints may bypass the token, but the bypass is explicit and counted — invisible free saves quietly delete the tension the tokens exist to create.

inputs.name: tokenItemId
inputs.description: Inventory item consumed per save. An item, not a counter, so tokens obey the same scarcity rules as everything else — inventory.scarcity_inventory will happily make you choose between a token and a herb.

inputs.name: tokensPerSave
inputs.description: Tokens consumed per write. Kept as an input because 'the final act costs two' is a legitimate escalation, and it should be a data change, not a patch.

inputs.name: savePointRequired
inputs.description: Whether saving only works at designated save-point volumes. The save-room is the genre's exhale — a lit room with a typewriter — and this flag is what protects it from becoming a menu item.

inputs.name: allowFreeAutosave
inputs.description: Whether checkpoint scripts may write without a token. Free autosaves are counted in savesMade with a flag on the event payload, so postmortems can tell player-earned saves from design-granted ones.

outputs.name: tokensRemaining
outputs.description: Live count of token items in inventory.core_inventory. Read, never cached — the inventory is the ledger.

outputs.name: savesMade
outputs.description: Lifetime successful writes this run. Rank screens and the genre's beloved 'S rank in under three saves' challenge both read this number.
